newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices drift lower in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices drift lower in quiet market.

text.p: Thai rubber prices drifted lower this week, pressured by ample supply and slow demand, trade sources said on Friday.
Traders said they were disappointed that the current low offer prices barely drew strong buying interest from Japan and China.
Buying from the United States was not expected in the market as the country was heard to be unwinding its big rubber stock.
"Buying from Japan was rather moderate and China is virtually absent from the market. The prices were also pressured by robust supplies," said one Hat Yai trader.
Thai rubber supplies entering the market this week rose 14.67 percent from last week to 58,719 kg, an auction market souce told Reuters.
Benchmark RSS3 for February shipment was quoted around $1.20 a kg FOB Bangkok. Some traders quoted as low as $1.18 a kg compared with $1.20-1.22 a kg last week.
STR20 was quoted around $1.18 a kg and latex dropped to $0.90 from $0.91-0.93 a kg on the same basis.
The market expected prices to firm in February when wintering in the south, Thailand's biggest rubber producing area, tightens supplies.- Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
